metadata.question: In the Norwegian Sea during Septermber 1, 2019, is the water color at (50.282684, -58.944881) more milky than (50.415337, -54.128047)?

data.raw_code: The user is asking about water color comparison in the Norwegian Sea on September 1, 2019, at two specific points. "Milky" water typically indicates higher turbidity or suspended sediments. For water color analysis, I should use: - Sentinel-2 MSI data (10-60m resolution) which has good water observation capabilities - Focus on bands that detect turbidity/sediments - typically the visible bands (blue, green, red) - A common approach is to use the Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI) = (Red - Green)/(Red + Green) - Higher NDTI values indicate more turbid/milky water Strategy: 1. Get Sentinel-2 imagery for the exact date and location 2. Calculate NDTI for both points 3. Compare the values to determine which is more "milky" I need to: - Define the two points as ee.Geometry.Point - Filter Sentinel-2 collection for the specific date and region - Check if images exist (handle C1 if not) - Calculate NDTI and extract values at both points - Validate the results and output appropriate answer ```javascript const ee = require('@google/earthengine'); const privateKey = require('../auth_keys/test-project-473922-29f05d49bed7'); async function runAnalysis() { // Define the two points in Norwegian Sea const point1 = ee.Geometry.Point([-58.944881, 50.282684]); const point2 = ee.Geometry.Point([-54.128047, 50.415337]); // Create a region around both points for filtering const region = ee.Geometry.BBox(-59.5, 50.0, -53.5, 50.8); // Date range - single day const startDate = '2019-09-01'; const endDate = '2019-09-02'; // Get Sentinel-2 surface reflectance collection const s2Col = ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED') .filterBounds(region) .filterDate(startDate, endDate) .filter(ee.Filter.lt('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', 80)); // Check if collection is empty const colSize = s2Col.size().getInfo(); console.log(`Sentinel-2 images found: ${colSize}`); if (colSize === 0) { console.log("C1"); return; } // Get the least cloudy image const image = s2Col.sort('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE').first(); // Calculate Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI) // NDTI = (Red - Green) / (Red + Green) // Higher values indicate more turbid/milky water const ndti = image.normalizedDifference(['B4', 'B3']).rename('NDTI'); // Extract NDTI values at both points const val1 = ndti.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.first(), geometry: point1, scale: 100, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('NDTI'); const val2 = ndti.reduceRegion({ reducer: ee.Reducer.first(), geometry: point2, scale: 100, maxPixels: 1e9 }).get('NDTI'); const ndti1 = val1.getInfo(); const ndti2 = val2.getInfo(); console.log(`Point 1 NDTI: ${ndti1 !== null ? ndti1.toFixed(4) : 'null'}`); console.log(`Point 2 NDTI: ${ndti2 !== null ? ndti2.toFixed(4) : 'null'}`); // Check for valid pixels if (ndti1 === null || ndti2 === null) { console.log("C2"); return; } // Check for invalid values if (Math.abs(ndti1) > 1 || Math.abs(ndti2) > 1 || isNaN(ndti1) || isNaN(ndti2)) { console.log("C3"); return; } // Compare values - higher NDTI means more turbid/milky water if (ndti1 > ndti2) { console.log("Point 1 has higher turbidity"); console.log("A"); } else { console.log("Point 2 has higher turbidity or equal"); console.log("B"); } } async function initEE() { await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.data.authenticateViaPrivateKey(privateKey, resolve, reject); }); await new Promise((resolve, reject) => { ee.initialize(null, null, resolve, reject); }); await runAnalysis(); } initEE(); ```
